The proposed priority order for evaluating different failure signals is as follows:  
1) Reachability DOWN (authoritative) => FAILOVER (unless no healthy fallback) [1].  
2) Errors (5xx) fast burn (high severity) => FAILOVER or PARTIAL_SHIFT depending on blast radius and capacity [1].  
3) Tail latency burn (p99/p95) => PARTIAL_SHIFT first; escalate to FAILOVER if corroborated and sustained [1].  
4) Capacity exhaustion / hard gate => HOLD + load shed (controller action), avoid shifting into constrained region [1].  
5) Control plane degradation => HOLD (do not flip rapidly; prevent oscillation) [1].

Reachability DOWN (authoritative) => FAILOVER (unless no healthy fallback) [1].
Errors (5xx) fast burn (high severity) => FAILOVER or PARTIAL_SHIFT depending on blast radius and capacity [1].
Tail latency burn (p99/p95) => PARTIAL_SHIFT first; escalate to FAILOVER if corroborated and sustained [1].

per_answer.answer: If the cache key canonicalization now treats a trailing slash differently between callers, it could lead to cache poisoning or silent correctness issues in a multi-customer environment. This is because different handling of trailing slashes can result in different cache keys for the same logical request, preventing cache hits and potentially serving incorrect data [1].
